title: Updates to MSA maps in FRED
gist: FRED is realigning its metropolitan statistical area (MSA) maps to the Census Bureau's July 2023 core-based statistical area delineations: micropolitan areas are dropped from the maps, 58 MSAs are renamed and 12 MSAs are added. Nine of the new MSAs are former micropolitan areas that graduated to metro status (e.g., Eagle Pass TX, Bozeman MT, Traverse City MI), a modest signal of where small-area population growth has crossed the 50,000 threshold.

themes.theme: FRED MSA map realignment to 2023 Census delineations

insights.claim: FRED's MSA maps are being updated to the US Census Bureau's July 2023 core-based statistical area delineations and will no longer show micropolitan statistical areas (urban clusters of 10,000-50,000 people), which previously appeared as gray 'no data' shading.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Anyone running regional screens or map-based dashboards off FRED loses visibility of sub-50k towns there; micro-area analysis must come from other Census sources.

insights.claim: Under the 2023 Census delineations, 58 MSAs in FRED have been renamed, e.g. 'Austin-Round Rock-Georgetown, TX' becomes 'Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos, TX' and 'Birmingham-Hoover, AL' becomes 'Birmingham, AL', so searches using old names may return no results.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Automated pipelines pulling FRED regional series by name should be checked for broken lookups after the rename.
insights.quote: Users searching for a familiar name might need to adjust their search terms if it no longer returns results.

insights.claim: Twelve MSAs are new in the 2023 delineations: three are entirely new metro areas (including Slidell-Mandeville-Covington, LA and Waterbury-Shelton, CT) and nine graduated from micropolitan to metropolitan status, such as Eagle Pass, TX, Bozeman, MT and Traverse City, MI.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Micro-to-metro graduations flag small markets whose urban-core population crossed 50,000 — a cue for regional housing, banking and retail growth stories, and new metro series with short histories.
